To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reversibility of aberrantly hypermethylated ER-alpha gene distinguishes precancer from cancer and that the reversibility is not observed for global DNA methylation.

global DNA and ER-a gene methylation are progressively enhanced during colorectal carcinogenesis and can be completely reversed by a NSAID celecoxib in APs, not in AdCa, and that global DNA methylation does not change with aging but ER-a gene methylations increases in the normal colorectal mucosae with aging, but this increase does not reach the level in APs.
the reversibility of aberrantly methylated global DNA and estrogen-receptor-alpha (ER-alpha) gene can be used as biomarkers for the differentiation between colorectal precancers and cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new concept of the clonal evolutionary model of colorectal cancer and the identification of novel biomarkers for the differentiation between precancer and cancer.
the development of cancer from precancer and its prevention by epigenetic therapy, which is a new strategy to treat cancer.
the identification of epigenetic biomarkers and the development of novel epigenetic therapies to prevent and/or treat colorectal cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aberrant epigenetic alteration in colorectal AP may be a reversible event, but that of AdCa is an irreversible event.

aberrant epigenetic alterations of DNA methylation in colorectal precancerous and cancerous lesions are not only reversible by a selective inhibitor of COX-2, but also distinguish colorectal precancer and cancer.
the aberrant global DNA hypomethylating and ER-alpha hypermethylation are reversible in precancer (APs) and irreversible in colorectal cancer (AdCa).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epigenome of cancer is not only a result of clonal evolutionary alterations, but also an important factor for the development of cancer.
epigenetic alterations in colorectal carcinogenesis are reversible in precancer, but irreversible in cancer.

cancer may arise through the following steps: TICs --> pCSC --> CSC --> cancer, and that the pCSC is a new type of tumor-initiating cells, which may be a potential target for early detection and treatment of colorectal cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reversibility of aberration in DNA methylation is an excellent biomarker for cancer development and for monitoring the efficacy of anti-cancer therapy, and that the aberrant DNA methyation in precancerous lesions may not be the cause of cancer, but may be a consequence of cancer initiation and/or progression.

aberrant global DNA methylation is a useful biomarker for the diagnosis of colorectal cancer, and that the reversibility of aberrantly methylated DNA is useful for the evaluation of the efficacy of anti-cancer therapy.
